WORSE THAN WRITTEN, and both belong in the fix:

1. THE BACKEND TOKEN EXPIRES FIRST. debugging.DEFAULT_LIFETIME_SECONDS is 3600 and the signature's clock starts at MINT; flag.LIFETIME is 3600s from LINK-OPEN. So the signature dies by however long the link sat in a chat channel before the volunteer tapped it. From that moment nginx's auth_request refuses every span post, and the SDK goes on batching and posting into 403s -- sdk.begin() built the exporter with wiring(token), so it holds the token captured at construction and cannot notice.

2. THE BADGE SAYS SO ON SCREEN. Its message is 'Recording this device for support. It stops on its own within the hour.' That is a promise made to the volunteer holding the phone, in words, which the code does not keep -- and Recording.tsx's own header calls this control 'non-negotiable rather than decorative'.

WHAT IS ALSO TRUE, and softens one point: at the client hour asked() calls forget(), so storage is cleared on the next API call and a reload does not resume recording. The leak is bounded by the page's life, not indefinite.

SCOPE UNCHANGED. The proposed fix -- one owner of the state in start.ts that Recording subscribes to, with expiry and the button tearing down through the same path -- still addresses all of it.
close_reason: Expiry and the button now take the same teardown, and the badge subscribes to the one owner of the answer.

title: Batch: the telemetry sweep, and the check that keeps it
description: The batch shipping inventory-tng-nb8.9, nb8.3, nb8.8, nb8.10 and nb8.11 -- the retroactive sweep over code written before the machinery existed, both halves of it, and the checker that stops it rotting. Membership only; what each issue is about is on the issue.
notes:
BATCH STATE, paused 2026-08-24.

Branch batch/telemetry-the-sweep, no pull request opened yet.

LANDED AND PUSHED, one commit each:
  nb8.9  Say what the backend is doing
  nb8.3  Record every function a request called
  nb8.8  Let a volunteer's browser say what happened
  nb8.10 Report what fails on a volunteer's phone

IN THE WORKING TREE, uncommitted: nb8.11. Its own notes carry exactly what is
written, what is left and the five failing cases in its test harness.

WHEN NB8.11 LANDS, the batch goes through the cycle in
.agents/skills/pull-requests/SKILL.md: push, open the draft, mark ready when
CI is green, post what the batch holds read off the commits, /code-review with
--comment, triage every finding to one issue before fixing any, fix in issue
order rebasing --autosquash between issues, then /simplify posting its findings
before applying them, resolve every thread, record the landing gate, merge
--rebase.

TWO HABITS THIS BATCH HAS ALREADY PAID FOR TWICE:
  - run scripts/check-docs.sh AFTER each commit as well as before; it reads
    git ls-files, so a new file's duplications are invisible until tracked.
  - the suite has to pass at EVERY commit, not only at the head, because main
    takes rebase merge. The recipe used last time is a detached worktree and a
    loop over 'git log --reverse --format=%h origin/main..HEAD'.
close_reason: Its last child landed; the batch goes through the review cycle from here.

title: check-docs.sh cannot read .env.sample or scripts/, and prose has been pasted into both
description:
Found in the review of pull request 19, and the reason it is one issue rather than a note against three: the same defect arrived in nb8.13, nb8.5 and nb8.4 because nothing could see it.

scripts/check-docs.sh builds its corpus from git ls-files over '*.md' '*.sh' '*.py' '*.yml' '*.yaml' '*.ts' '*.tsx'. .env.sample matches none of those, and neither does an extensionless executable under scripts/ -- scripts/pretty-logs and scripts/ship-logs are both unread. AGENTS.md calls rule 1 non-negotiable and the checker that enforces it has a hole exactly where configuration is explained.

MEASURED: copying .env.sample to a .py extension and running the checker reports 11 repetitions on this branch against 2 on main, including a 23-word run shared with docs/deployment.md.

TWO HALVES, and the second is what stops it recurring: trim the duplications so each explanation is in one place and the others link to it, and teach check-docs.sh to read .env.sample and the extensionless files under scripts/. The corpus is stated as what is NOT read for exactly this reason -- see the comment above the git ls-files call -- so the fix belongs there rather than in a list of extra paths.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/check-docs.sh reads .env.sample and every file under scripts/, and is clean. The repetitions it then finds are gone rather than allowed, unless check-docs.allow says why.
close_reason: check-docs.sh reads every tracked file that is prose, .env.sample and scripts/ included, and the nineteen repetitions that surfaced are gone.

title: Batch: a collector to send to, and what may reach it
description: The batch shipping inventory-tng-nb8.13, nb8.5, nb8.6, nb8.7 and nb8.4: the work that makes pointing this application at a collector a safe thing to do. Membership only -- what each issue is about is on the issue.
close_reason: All children completed

title: An empty environment variable is not an unset one, for the eight settings that still have the sharp edge
description:
Found by the quality pass on pull request 17, which fixed it for five variables and left the rest.

THE DEFECT. django-environ applies a default only when a variable is ABSENT. A variable set to the empty string is present, so env() hands back '' and whatever parses it raises at settings import -- taking down check, migrate, collectstatic, runserver and the whole test run, with a traceback that never names the file that caused it.

TWO WAYS TO REACH IT, both ordinary. A developer clears a value in .env rather than deleting the line; .env.sample all but invites it, shipping several variables empty. Or a values file blanks a chart setting: infra/helm/inventory-tng/templates/_helpers.tpl emits NUM_PROXIES, APPEND_BURST_RATE, APPEND_SUSTAINED_RATE, REAUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, LABEL_BASE_URL and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS whether or not they have anything to say, so numProxies: "" is int('') at import and a CrashLoopBackOff with an invisible cause.

WHERE IT STANDS. There are now three treatments of one problem in this repository: inventory_tng/hosts.py strips empties for its two variables, inventory_tng/options.py defaults them for the five telemetry ones, and the rest get nothing. That is the reason to do this -- not the individual crashes, but that a reader has no rule for which behaviour a given setting has.

THE SHAPE. One accessor everything uses: an environ.Env subclass, or a thin wrapper, that treats a present-but-empty value as absent WHENEVER A DEFAULT EXISTS. DJANGO_SECRET_KEY deliberately has none and must keep raising -- that distinction is the whole design and must survive. Then options.py folds back into the same declaration block as everything else and stops being a special case.

Its docstring points here, so closing this means editing that too.
close_reason: environment.Env reads through a view in which an empty variable is absent; options.missing is the shared predicate

title: Frontend: instrument the code that already exists
description:
The retroactive sweep for the frontend, which Ali asked to be one bead.

The scanner and its decode loop, which is where failures actually happen and where the single console.error lives; the batch outbox and what it does when a submission cannot be sent; label printing; and the API layer, so a failed request is attributable to what the person was doing rather than to a URL.

Browser telemetry has a constraint the backend does not: it costs the volunteer's battery and data, on a phone in a basement. So the ordinary path is spans only under a sampled trace, while errors and a small number of counters are always reported. That asymmetry needs stating in the code, because it is the kind of thing a later change quietly removes.

Depends on the frontend OTel issue for the machinery.
acceptance_criteria: A scan failure, a failed submission and a print failure are each diagnosable from telemetry. Nothing is exported for an unsampled session beyond errors. No personal data is attached.
close_reason: The scanner, the outbox and the API layer report what fails; spans only under a flagged session, failures always, and the asymmetry stated in report.ts. The third credential-free endpoint is argued in decision 0012.

title: Frontend: OpenTelemetry in the browser, and the debug flag that turns it on
description:
The SPA produces no telemetry today. Its one console.error runs on a volunteer's phone and is seen by nobody.

PACKAGES: @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-web, @opentelemetry/instrumentation-fetch, @opentelemetry/instrumentation-document-load, @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http, and a context manager so async work stays in its span.

PROPAGATION is the point. instrumentation-fetch puts traceparent on every call to /api, nginx forwards it untouched (no underscore in the name, so it is not dropped), and the backend's sampler reads it. /api is same-origin behind the frontend's nginx, so no CORS and no propagateTraceHeaderCorsUrls -- that knob becomes necessary only if the API ever moves to another host.

THE CSP CONSTRAINT, decided. frontend/nginx.conf.template sets connect-src 'self', so a browser exporter pointed at another origin is blocked outright. Rather than widen the policy, nginx proxies a same-origin path to the collector: policy untouched, no preflight, collector never internet-facing. That path needs the guard in the debug-token issue.

THE FLAG: ?trace=1 in the URL, persisted with an expiry, with a visible indicator so nobody leaves it on. An administrator can send a volunteer a link. It sets the sampled bit, which is what makes one click produce a single trace through nginx, Django and psycopg.

ALSO window.onerror and unhandledrejection, which is the whole of the frontend's error reporting today.
acceptance_criteria: A click with the flag on produces one trace containing browser spans and the server spans beneath them. With the flag off, nothing is exported. The CSP is unchanged. The flag expires by itself.
notes:
WHAT NB8.4 LEFT FOR THIS ISSUE, and it is not optional.

The token exists and the backend honours it: inventory_tng/debugging.py mints one (manage.py mint_debug_token), a WSGI wrapper checks the X-Debug-Trace header before Django sees the request, and the sampler records that request in full whatever the rate says. What is missing is the browser end, which is this issue: the flag that makes the SPA send the header, and the SPA's own exporter.

THE INGEST PATH IS THIS ISSUE'S TO GUARD. nb8.4's acceptance named it and nb8.4 deliberately did not build it, because a proxy location with nothing posting to it and no consumer would be an unauthenticated write path shipped ahead of any need for it. Build it here, with the browser exporter it exists for, and give it all of:

- the same X-Debug-Trace token required on the POST, verified before anything is proxied. inventory_tng.debugging.minted is the check; an unverified post is refused rather than forwarded.
- nginx limit_req on that location. A browser exporter posts in batches and a page reloaded in a loop must not become a write amplifier.
- client_max_body_size on it, small. An OTLP batch from one page is kilobytes.
- the frontend's connect-src stays 'self' -- epic point 8 -- so the exporter posts to a same-origin path and nginx forwards it. Do not widen that policy.

Also worth knowing before starting: the browser's sampled bit is not authority on its own. The backend puts a remote sampled parent through the same ratio, so browser and backend running the same rate agree about a trace without either trusting the other. The token is what raises the rate, at both ends.

docs/observability.md#recording-one-volunteers-requests says the browser half is not built yet and prints the curl in its place. That paragraph goes when this lands.
close_reason: The SPA traces under a signed token from a link, propagates traceparent to the backend, reports uncaught failures, shows a badge with a Stop, and posts to a same-origin path nginx guards with auth_request, a rate and a body cap.

title: Backend: instrument the code that already exists
description:
The retroactive sweep for the backend, which Ali asked to be one bead.

Everything before this adds the machinery; this puts it through the code that was written without it. Working from what the system actually does rather than from a file list: the ledger append path and every reason it rejects; minting, printing and revoking labels; the sheet importer's stages, which already have a staged-then-committed shape worth counting; volunteer identity resolution and merging; sign-in, second factor and step-up; and the management commands, which run unattended and today say nothing about what they did.

Both halves, per Ali: a log at the right level, and a metric where it is a state change somebody would page on. The metrics named in the epic belong here.

The test of this issue is not coverage but a question: when a volunteer says an append did not work, can you find out why without reproducing it?
acceptance_criteria: Each area above emits logs and metrics. A rejected append is diagnosable from telemetry alone. No personal data reaches an exporter, checked against the redaction allowlist.
notes:
WHAT A REQUEST'S LOG LINES CAN AND CANNOT CARRY, measured 2026-08-23 against a real server with the collector of inventory-tng-nb8.6 in front of it.

A record written INSIDE a request carries trace_id and span_id and is findable from the span -- verified: a log call inside an active span comes out with both filled.

A record Django writes about a 4xx or a 5xx does NOT, and cannot. log_response for those is called from BaseHandler.get_response AFTER self._middleware_chain(request) has returned, so the OpenTelemetry middleware has already ended and detached its span. Every django.request record therefore has an empty trace_id, and so does every access line -- runserver's and gunicorn's alike, both of which are outside the application entirely.

The consequence for this issue: the only way a request's own story is followable from its trace is for the APPLICATION to write it, from inside the view or the serializer. Django's own records will not do it, and neither will a middleware placed outside OpenTelemetry's. A request-scoped record bound in middleware has to be emitted from inside the chain, beneath the instrumentation, to be worth anything.

docs/observability.md says this to a reader; it is here because it decides where this issue's log calls go.
close_reason: Every area named emits records and a counter; a request writes its own record from inside the chain, so it carries a trace id and a request id and the rest of that request's records share the id.

title: Backend: record every function invoked, at DEBUG and inside a sampled trace
description:
Ali's requirement: at DEBUG level, a log should name every single function that was invoked, and new code has to keep satisfying that.

THE MECHANISM, proposed: a @traced decorator that opens a span, plus a sweep applied once per module at app ready() that wraps the callables a module exports. Not sys.setprofile, which costs an order of magnitude and reaches into the standard library; not AST rewriting, which is unreadable when it goes wrong.

WHY SPANS RATHER THAN LOG LINES. 'Which functions ran, in what order, and how long each took' is what a trace already is, and it nests, which a flat log line cannot. The DEBUG log view is then a projection of the span stream rather than a second mechanism that can disagree with it.

TWO SWITCHES, and they matter. Globally at DEBUG for development. Per request for everything else -- a trace the client marked debug records fine-grained spans for that request alone, so the same detail is available in a deployed system without turning it on for all traffic. That is the same flag the frontend sets.

SCOPE HAS TO BE CHOSEN. Wrapping every callable in inventory/ includes serializer field access and other hot paths; expect a real cost and measure it before choosing packages. Model methods and properties, classmethods, and descriptors all need care -- a naive wrap breaks Django's metaclasses.
acceptance_criteria: At DEBUG every call in the covered packages appears with its caller and duration. Overhead when disabled is measured and recorded. A test proves a nested call appears nested. The covered package list is explicit, not implied.
close_reason: A @traced wrapper and a sweep at ready(), over an explicit module list; two switches; the overhead measured and recorded; a test proving a nested call nests.

title: Backend: a signed, expiring debug token so a client cannot decide what is recorded
description:
The frontend debug flag works by setting the W3C sampled bit, which a ParentBased sampler honours. Taken literally that hands an unauthenticated client control of backend telemetry volume: anyone can send traceparent with sampled=1 on every request.

THE SHAPE. An administrator mints a short-lived token; django.core.signing.TimestampSigner does it in about fifteen lines, with expiry and revocation by key rotation. The volunteer receives it in a link. The SPA sends it as a header, and a custom sampler honours the incoming sampled bit only when the token verifies.

RATE LIMIT ON TOP, because a valid token should not be able to cost unbounded telemetry either. inventory/throttling.py is the existing pattern for exactly this problem -- decision 0012 rate limits the endpoints that take no credential, and debug tracing is another write that takes none.

THE OTLP PATH NEEDS ITS OWN GUARD. The browser exporter posts to a same-origin path proxied to the collector, which is an unauthenticated ingest endpoint unless it requires the same token. nginx limit_req and a body size cap belong here too.

Why this rather than restricting the flag to administrators: volunteers do not sign in (decision 0012) and are the people who meet the failures, so an administrators-only flag debugs only the sessions that were never the problem.
acceptance_criteria: An unsigned or expired token means the sampled bit is ignored. A valid one is honoured within a rate limit. The OTLP ingest path refuses an unauthenticated post. A metric counts debug-sampled requests so abuse is visible.
notes:
A SECOND THING THIS TOKEN COULD GATE, worth deciding here rather than assuming.

inventory-tng-nb8.5 gains a toggle that lets telemetry carry personal data --
IP addresses above all -- because that is what somebody debugging a throttle or
one volunteer'''s failing request actually needs to see. As specified there it is
an environment variable: process-wide, on until somebody turns it off, and
therefore the kind of thing that gets left on.

This token is process-independent, per-request and expiring, which is the shape
a production one-off wants: turn it on for the request you are chasing, and have
it stop being on by itself. If the token can carry that permission alongside the
debug-tracing one, say so and record why; if it should not -- because widening
what one signed token authorises is its own risk -- record that instead.

Either way nb8.5 owes the environment toggle, which is what a developer with a
collector in front of them needs. This is about the production path only.
close_reason: Signed, expiring token; a WSGI guard before Django; the sampler honours a proven request; rate limited per token; a metric by outcome. The OTLP ingest guard is recorded on nb8.8, which builds the path it guards.

title: The documented rebase hangs a non-interactive session
description:
DEVELOPERS.md:1142, .agents/skills/pull-requests/SKILL.md:106 and scripts/check-batch.sh:332 all print:

  git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main

AGENTS.md's Shell section forbids interactive flags for exactly this reason: -i spawns $GIT_EDITOR on the todo list, which never returns without a human, and the branch is left mid-rebase so the retry fails with 'rebase in progress'.

This matters more now that AGENTS.md lets an agent run the collapse and merge unattended. The non-interactive form is:

  git -c sequence.editor=true rebase --autosquash origin/main

Pre-existing in all three files, which is why it is its own issue rather than a passenger on inventory-tng-y26: one change, three files, one topic.
acceptance_criteria: No document or script prints 'rebase -i' as a command to run. The form given completes without a human. The three files agree.
close_reason: All three places now print 'git -c sequence.editor=true rebase --autosquash origin/main', verified to fold a fixup and exit 0 with no editor on git 2.55. check-batch.test.sh asserts the advice it prints carries sequence.editor and never 'rebase -i'.

title: Let an agent merge a batch when every merge requirement is already met
description:
CLAUDE.md puts merging under 'ask first, every time'. That was the right default when nothing mechanical checked the cycle had been run; it no longer is. Merging is now the most heavily gated action in the repository and the least discretionary:

- .claude/hooks/landing-gate.sh refuses gh pr merge until the review cycle is recorded against the exact head being merged
- main requires every CI check green, a linear history, the branch up to date, and every conversation resolved
- scripts/check-batch.sh refuses a branch whose commits do not map one-to-one onto issues

By the time all of those are satisfied there is nothing left for a human to decide, and the approval step costs a round trip at the one moment the work is finished and verified. Ali granted this permanently on 2026-08-22, having previously granted it per-run.

What stays behind an ask does not change: anything touching main directly, a bare push --force, bd dolt push, and any change to repository or branch settings.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md's table moves merging to the without-asking row, conditioned on the requirements being met, and says which gates make it safe. The ask-first row keeps everything else. DEVELOPERS.md#merging is not duplicated -- CLAUDE.md links to it.
close_reason: Closed

title: CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS has the unstripped-list trap ALLOWED_HOSTS just had fixed
description:
django-environ's list cast is split(',') with no strip, so 'a, b' yields ' b' -- a value that matches nothing and is invisible in a values file because the space does not show.

inventory-tng-adj fixed this for DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS by stripping once in inventory_tng/hosts.py. CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is read with the same (list, []) cast one screen below in settings.py, is fed from django.corsAllowedOrigins and from .env.sample, and has the identical trap with the identical invisibility. Nothing else in settings.py uses a list cast today, so this is the second and last site.

Found by the /simplify altitude pass on PR #14, which made the point that the branch named the trap eloquently and left it next door.

Fix at the mechanism rather than the variable: one helper both list-valued reads go through, so a third list cast added later gets it for free.
acceptance_criteria: A comma-separated CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS with spaces yields trimmed origins; a test covers it; every (list, []) read in settings.py goes through the same helper.
close_reason: Env.parse_value trims every list cast, so both list-valued reads and any third go through inventory_tng.environment.entries.

title: check-docs.sh cannot read the chart's templates, and DEVELOPERS.md says it can
description:
scripts/check-docs.sh globs '*.md *.sh *.py *.yml *.yaml *.ts *.tsx'. infra/helm/inventory-tng/templates/_helpers.tpl matches none of them, so the one file in the chart that holds prose is the one file rule 1 is not enforced over.

DEVELOPERS.md#documentation-rules states the checker reads the chart's templates and enumerates the exclusions as only nginx.conf.template and the Dockerfiles. That is wrong today.

Demonstrated during the /simplify pass on PR #14: run by hand over the two files it cannot pair, the checker fails on a 13-word repeat between settings.py and _helpers.tpl that the full run reports clean.

Fix: add '*.tpl' to the corpus glob, correct the exclusion list in DEVELOPERS.md, and expect the existing prose to need a pass before it goes green.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/check-docs.sh reads *.tpl; DEVELOPERS.md's exclusion list matches the glob; the full run is green.
close_reason: The corpus half was already fixed by the rewrite to 'every tracked file less what is not prose' -- _helpers.tpl, the Dockerfiles, nginx.conf.template and .env.sample are all read, verified. What remained was DEVELOPERS.md still describing the old seven-extension list and naming exclusions that no longer exist. Five cases now pin the corpus so a return to naming extensions is a red suite.

title: Sign in once for the whole browser suite
description:
Found by the simplify pass on PR #13, 2026-08-22.

frontend/playwright.config.ts runs one worker, and there are now six signIn() calls across five spec files: api-reachable (twice), decodes, offline-batch, sign-in, and the new guide-controls. The server accepts a TOTP code once per 30-second window, so integration/sign-in.ts polls authenticatorCode every 2 seconds for up to 40 seconds when a code is spent. Any sign-in landing in the same window as the last pays 0-30 seconds, mean about 15.

That 40-second poll lives inside a 90-second per-test timeout. It is the likeliest way this suite goes red for no reason, which matters more than the minute it costs.

FIX: a Playwright setup project, or a globalSetup that opens a browser, does the real password-and-TOTP sign-in once and writes storageState; every spec but sign-in.spec.ts declares use: { storageState }. sign-in.spec.ts keeps the real flow, because that is the thing it tests. Removes five of six sign-ins, every window collision and every poll.

SMALLER, ADJACENT: sign-in.ts's poll re-derives the code by spawning Python every 2 seconds. TOTP boundaries are deterministic -- 30 - (Date.now()/1000 % 30) gives the exact wait -- so one sleep and one compute would do. Only worth touching if storageState is rejected.

title: Let the label list be narrowed to a shelf, an item or a print run
description:
Found by an inventory administrator on 2026-08-22, trying to do the job guides/administrator.md sets: print labels for a shelf, and replace a faded batch as a set.

LabelAdmin has list_display but no list_filter, and search_fields is ['code'] -- searching by the one thing you are trying to find out. There is no date_hierarchy on printed_at. So collecting the codes for one shelf means sorting by a column and reading them off by eye, and 'the date is there so a faded batch can be found and replaced as a set' is not achievable on any screen.

The guide has been corrected to say what is possible today. This is the change that makes the sentence worth writing properly.

FIX: list_filter on item, location and printed_at, and search_fields extended to item__name and location__name. Small, and it turns two impossible tasks into two clicks.

title: The migrate Job has no resources, so a quota rejects it
description:
Found by a deployment review on 2026-08-22, verified in rendered output.

infra/helm/inventory-tng/templates/migrate-job.yaml renders with no resources block at all, while backend-deployment.yaml has one. On any shared cluster with a ResourceQuota requiring requests.cpu and requests.memory -- the normal case when somebody has 'been given a namespace' -- the Job pod is rejected outright. It is a pre-install hook, so Helm blocks on a Job that will never run, times out, and fails the install. The error names a pod that no longer exists.

Two smaller things in the same file: it sets readOnlyRootFilesystem without the /tmp emptyDir the backend gets, and the revision-suffixed name with hook-delete-policy before-hook-creation means completed Jobs accumulate for ever, since that policy only removes a resource of the same name.

FIX: give the Job the backend's resources stanza and its /tmp mount.
notes:
SIMPLIFY PASS, 2026-08-22 — the altitude arm argues this is the one of the four documented chart defects that should be fixed in the chart rather than written up, and the argument is worth keeping:

migrate-job.yaml has no resources block, while backend-deployment.yaml already interpolates .Values.backend.resources from a value the chart carries. So the fix is ONE LINE of the same template expression, strictly additive, invisible on any cluster without a quota -- and provable by 'helm template | grep' in the CI step PR #13 just added.

The other three (adj, uq6, qe7) are correctly documented rather than fixed: qe7 is release engineering, uq6 needs a backend endpoint that does not touch the database, adj is a behaviour change to a chart nothing in CI can install. This one is different in kind, and documenting a defect you could have fixed for less effort than the paragraph took is the shallow call.

Not done in PR #13 because fixing one of four arbitrarily is less coherent than fixing none in a documentation batch. Whoever picks this up: it is smaller than it looks.
close_reason: The migrate Job declares migrations.resources, so a namespace with a ResourceQuota admits it. Held by a chart test asserting every rendered container declares a cpu and memory request, mutation-checked by taking the Job's away.

title: Stop the chart doubling its own name into every resource
description:
inventory-tng.fullname is 'printf %s-%s .Release.Name (chart name)' with no check for the release name already containing the chart name -- the collapse every scaffolded Helm chart carries. The documented install names the release inventory-tng, so every resource renders as inventory-tng-inventory-tng-backend.

WHY THIS IS BEING FIXED NOW RATHER THAN DEFERRED, which reverses the reasoning this bead was opened with. It was opened saying the chart half 'renames live resources, so it is a release-time decision'. There are no live resources: inventory-tng-qe7 records that nothing has ever published an image and there are no tags, so this chart has never been installed anywhere. The rename is free today and will never be cheaper.

Left alone it also rots the documentation that inventory-tng-61c just corrected. Four kubectl commands in docs/deployment.md name the rendered resources, and when this lands all four become silently wrong -- test_documented_commands.py holds documented chart VALUES against values.yaml, but nothing holds documented resource NAMES against what the chart renders. That is the gap that let the original wrong names ('deploy/inventory-tng-backend', which never existed) survive in the first place.

So the fix is three things, not one:
1. the contains collapse in _helpers.tpl
2. the four kubectl lines in docs/deployment.md, back to the name a reader would guess
3. a check that holds the two together, so the next edit to either cannot drift
close_reason: Closed

title: Give the backend a writable HOME so gunicorn's control socket works in the cluster
description:
gunicorn 26 opens a control socket under the account's home directory. The backend Deployment and the migrate Job run with readOnlyRootFilesystem and mount an emptyDir at /tmp only, so every backend pod logs 'Control server error: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: /home/app/.gunicorn' at ERROR on start and runs without one.

Seen while hardening compose.yaml for inventory-tng-61c, where the fix was a tmpfs at /home/app. The chart wants the same: an emptyDir mounted at /home/app on infra/helm/inventory-tng/templates/backend-deployment.yaml.

A first log line that is an ERROR teaches whoever is watching a rollout to skim past errors, which is the actual cost.

title: DESIGN: one product, one spelling, and comparisons that ignore case
description:
Raised by the project owner on 2026-08-22 while reviewing rule 1.

THE PROPOSAL, in their words: keep the original format, spelling and letter case when it is free text; but for structured data, compare case-insensitively everywhere, so a pulldown or an autocomplete cannot offer the same product under three spellings. The spelling shown must be the one the manufacturer intends -- MacBook Pro, not macBook pro or Macbook Pro. Typing on a keyboard must stay easy. They asked for research into what could go wrong with it before anything is built.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, so the proposal is a refinement rather than a new direction: Item.name holds the canonical spelling, ItemIdentifier.value preserves whatever was typed, and ItemIdentifier.value_normalised is a Lower(Trim()) generated column with a unique index. The rule that follows from it is 'search identifiers, display items' -- a pulldown showing identifier values is what produces the three-spellings problem.

WHAT THE RESEARCH IS FOR, three strands run 2026-08-22:
  1. Codebase: every place text is folded, every uniqueness constraint on a text field, and above all whether a typed or scanned string can reach a pulldown where the canonical name belongs.
  2. PostgreSQL 18, tested rather than recalled: whether Python str.lower() can disagree with the database's lower() -- because a Python-side duplicate check and a database unique index that disagree produce a 500 rather than a clean refusal; whether a nondeterministic ICU collation beats the generated column; and critically whether such a collation forbids LIKE and prefix matching, which would foreclose autocomplete.
  3. The real data: six candidate foldings over the 52 catalogue names and the 145 typed strings, looking for merges that are wrong. Case is the easy axis. This catalogue already holds RJ45 passthrough, RJ-45 Coupler (Indoors) and TP-Link SFP-RJ45, so a case-only rule still misses; a punctuation-folding rule risks merging products that genuinely differ.

KNOWN HAZARD ALREADY OBSERVED THIS SESSION: casefold() and lower() disagree on the German sharp s, and items.normalised was deliberately changed from casefold() to lower() to match the Lower(Trim()) column. Any new rule has to keep the Python side and the database side saying the same thing.

This wants a decision record in docs/decisions/ -- future readers will ask why -- and the implementation is a separate bead once the record is agreed.
design:
RESEARCH STRAND 3, THE REAL DATA — measured 2026-08-22 against the 52 catalogue names and 145 distinct typed strings. This is the strand that settles how hard to fold.

THE HEADLINE: zero catalogue collisions under EVERY rule tested, up to and including 'strip everything but [0-9a-z]'. All 52 names stay 52 distinct folded forms. Netpower 15R and Netpower 16P stay apart at every level.

AGGRESSIVE FOLDING BUYS ALMOST NOTHING HERE. Newly resolving typed strings, for all seven rules: 0. The 56 unresolved strings are 49 opaque retired NYCM SKU codes, 6 genuinely ambiguous (mast, rj45, Omni), and 4 that are not products. None is a spacing or punctuation variant of a catalogue name, so no fold can reach them. Coverage by pure fold: raw 52 strings, lower() 61, most aggressive 64 -- a gain of 3 strings and 4 submissions over lower().

TRIM, WHITESPACE-COLLAPSE AND NFKC ARE PROVABLE NO-OPS on this corpus: lower() == lower().strip() == collapsed == NFKC for all 197 strings. No leading/trailing space, no doubled space, no tab, no NBSP, nothing NFKC changes. They cost nothing either.

CASE-ONLY FOLDING IS SAFE AND IS WHAT THE DATA ASKS FOR. lower() collapses the 145 typed strings to 134 in 9 groups, none of them a bad merge, none spanning two catalogue targets -- LiteBeam/Litebeam/litebeam, Mast straight/mast straight/Mast Straight, OmniTikPOE/OmnitikPOE, Tp-Link/Tp-link, and five more. That is exactly the owner's stated goal.

HEADROOM: the catalogue's tightest distinguishing feature is a 2-character difference in a model number. Zero pairs at Levenshtein 1; minimum pairwise distance is 2, and folding does not tighten it. The seven closest pairs are all genuinely different products (15m/30m fiber, SC-APC/LC-UPC, Netpower 15R/16P, UAP-AC-M/IW, CubeSA/Cube). SO: any canonicalisation is safe, but a rule that folded digits, dropped short tokens, or used an edit-distance threshold of 2 or more would immediately merge real products. Fuzzy matching must never decide identity -- only suggest.

CHARACTERS: the catalogue is 100 percent ASCII. Exactly one non-ASCII character in the entire corpus, a right single quotation mark, in the one prose string no rule can resolve and which is already in UNRESOLVABLE.

THE FINDING THAT BEARS HARDEST ON THE OWNER'S REQUEST: 'spelling as the manufacturer intends' is NOT true of the catalogue today. It is wrong in at least six places -- Tp-Link should be TP-Link, OmniTikPOE should be OmniTIK PoE, Hex POE should be hEX PoE, Netpower should be netPower, ToughCable should be TOUGHCable -- and it contradicts itself: Ubiquiti J-Pole against Jpole Umount Extender, RJ45 against RJ-45. Eleven names carry intercaps that lower() would visibly destroy if it were ever used for display; ten are casually typed (mast straight, RJ45 passthrough, W-mounts). So making the catalogue canonical is a DATA task with an owner, not only a code change, and it needs somebody who can say what each manufacturer's spelling is.
acceptance_criteria:
THE PLAN, from the three research strands. Each step is its own bead when this is agreed; this one is the decision record.

DECISION 1 — KEEP THE GENERATED COLUMN. Not a nondeterministic ICU collation, not citext. It is the only one of the three with a SOUND indexed prefix search, which autocomplete needs. The collation is otherwise the better mechanism and PostgreSQL's own documentation prefers it over citext, so the record must say plainly that it was rejected for the pg_trgm unsoundness rather than because it is worse.

DECISION 2 — FIX THE EXPRESSION, which is where the real defects are. LOWER(TRIM(value)) becomes, in order: NFC-normalise, strip the whitespace TRIM does not (tab, CR, LF, NBSP, and the other invisibles), collapse internal whitespace runs to one space, then lower. Every function needed is IMMUTABLE and legal in a generated column. This closes three holes the current constraint has: the decomposed-accent duplicate, the tab-and-NBSP duplicates, and the double-internal-space duplicate.

DECISION 3 — FOLD CASE AND WHITESPACE, NOTHING ELSE. Do NOT fold punctuation. The data says so: zero catalogue collisions under any rule, but folding harder buys 3 strings and 4 submissions, while the catalogue's tightest distinguishing feature is a 2-character difference in a model number. Every unresolved string is an opaque SKU, an ambiguous word or not a product -- none is a punctuation variant. RJ-45 against RJ45 was a hazard I imagined; the data does not have it.

DECISION 4 — THE PYTHON SIDE IS NOT AN AUTHORITY. PG lower() and Python str.lower() disagree, in both directions, and cannot be reconciled. So: the database constraint decides, IntegrityError is a normal outcome to be reported as a clean conflict rather than a 500, and the Python normaliser exists only to make the common case fast and must never be the thing that decides two strings are one. Say this in the code, next to the function.

DECISION 5 — SEARCH IDENTIFIERS, DISPLAY ITEMS. This is the rule that answers the owner's actual concern about a pulldown offering one product three times. It needs the codebase survey to confirm nothing currently leaks -- that strand was stopped before it reported and must be re-run.

DECISION 6 — AUTOCOMPLETE NEEDS AN INDEX THE SCHEMA DOES NOT HAVE. Add text_pattern_ops on the normalised column, and lower the search term in Python before querying with __startswith. Django's __istartswith compiles to UPPER(col) LIKE UPPER(...) and is unindexable -- it must not be used on this path.

DECISION 7 — THE CANONICAL SPELLING IS A DATA TASK WITH AN OWNER. The catalogue is wrong in at least six places against the manufacturers and contradicts itself in two more. No code change makes 'the spelling the manufacturer intends' true. This needs somebody who can say what each one is, and it is not the same piece of work as the normalisation.

MIGRATION RISK TO STATE IN THE RECORD: changing the generated expression rewrites the column and may surface duplicates the old constraint let through. The migration has to find them first and report them, not fail halfway.
notes:
RESEARCH STRAND 2, POSTGRESQL 18.6 TESTED — 2026-08-22. Database is UTF8,
datcollate en_US.UTF-8, provider libc, deterministic.

1. PG lower() DISAGREES WITH PYTHON str.lower() on 3 of 24 inputs, and the
disagreements are the load-bearing ones. Split-brain pairs, verified against an
exact replica of ItemIdentifier:
  - 'IPHONE' vs 'İPHONE' (U+0130): PG says SAME, Python says DIFFERENT. PG maps
    İ to i; Python maps it to i + U+0307.
  - 'ΟΔΟΣ' vs 'οδος' with final sigma: PG says DIFFERENT, Python says SAME.
  casefold() is a fourth answer again (9 of 24 differ from PG). Under a Turkish
  ICU collation lower('IPHONE') is 'ıphone' -- the opposite direction. lower()
  is collation-dependent; Python's is not.
  CONSEQUENCE: a Python pre-check and the database unique index cannot be made
  to agree. Any check-then-insert path must treat IntegrityError as a NORMAL
  outcome, not an assertion failure.

2. THE CURRENT COLUMN IS NORMALISATION-BLIND. Two rows both accepted, rendering
identically, differing only in byte length: 'Café' as U+00E9 and as e+U+0301.
normalize(value, NFC) IS IMMUTABLE and closes it inside the generated column --
verified. unaccent() is STABLE, so it is foreclosed from generated columns.

3. TRIM() STRIPS ASCII SPACE AND NOTHING ELSE. Verified against the replica:
tab-padded, double-internal-space, NBSP, ZWSP, narrow NBSP, ideographic space,
BOM and soft hyphen ALL defeat the unique constraint. Four visually identical
rows were accepted, three of them duplicates the constraint exists to stop.
btrim(x, ' \t\r\n' + U+00A0) and regexp_replace are both IMMUTABLE, so the fix
is available.

4. NONDETERMINISTIC ICU COLLATION: rejected, and the reason is subtle. It does
work -- '=' becomes case- and NFC-insensitive, the unique index rejects
'macbook pro' against 'MacBook Pro' and keeps the manufacturer's spelling in one
column with no application code. In PG 18 even LIKE works and is
collation-aware. BUT a pg_trgm index CAN be created on such a column, the
planner WILL use it, and pg_trgm is not collation-aware -- the same query
returned 1 row on a seq scan and 0 rows through the index. Silent wrong answers.
ILIKE, all regex, starts_with, ^@ and text_pattern_ops are refused outright. The
escape hatch, a functional index cast back to COLLATE C, reintroduces lower()
for search while uniqueness keeps ICU semantics -- two different notions of
sameness in one table.

5. CITEXT: rejected. PostgreSQL 18's own documentation opens by recommending
nondeterministic collations instead, and its Limitations section says it is not
truly case-insensitive by Unicode's definition. It IS lower(), so it inherits
every problem in (1) and (2). Worse: no index can serve a prefix query on it --
both text_pattern_ops and gin_trgm_ops create, and neither is ever used, because
the operator resolved is citext ~~ citext.

6. DJANGO: db_collation= works and a UniqueConstraint inherits it;
CreateCollation is a first-class migration operation. Lower()/Trim() compile to
plain lower()/TRIM() with no COLLATE. A GeneratedField with a non-immutable
function is NOT caught by makemigrations -- it ships in a committed migration
and fails at migrate time. Only __regex/__iregex are foreclosed by a
nondeterministic collation.

7. INDEXES, measured on 6000 rows. The current design needs an index it does not
have: the unique default-ops btree CANNOT serve a prefix query (seq scan, 5900
rows filtered) because the database is en_US and not C. A separate
text_pattern_ops index makes it a bitmap index scan. AND Django's __istartswith
compiles to UPPER(col) LIKE UPPER(pattern), which matches NO index on any of the
three designs -- only a plain __startswith against an already-lowercased pattern
uses the index.



RESEARCH STRAND 1, THE CODEBASE — surveyed 2026-08-22, re-run after the
first attempt was stopped. Read-only survey of backend and frontend.

1. NOTHING LEAKS TODAY, and the answer is exhaustive rather than a spot
check. ItemIdentifier is not reachable through the API at all: serializers.py
and views.py never import it, there is no ItemIdentifierSerializer and no
endpoint returns one. Every list endpoint returns a canonical name --
Item.name, Location.name, Category.name, Volunteer.display_name -- and
LabelMapSerializer goes out of its way to send item_name from item.name. No
model has a ForeignKey to ItemIdentifier, so Django never renders its __str__
(which does start with the raw value) inside a select.

The frontend has NO MUI Autocomplete at all, no datalist and no bare select.
Every option list renders a stored canonical field: LocationPicker renders
location.name, ItemRow renders item.name, VolunteerPicker renders
display_name. The only raw typed strings on screen are the two empty-state
sentences and VolunteerPicker's 'Add <typed>' affordance, which is the free
text the owner's proposal permits.

The Django admin already implements the proposed rule in the one place
identifiers are searchable: ItemAdmin.search_fields includes
identifiers__value while list_display shows name. Search identifiers, display
items -- already true, by accident rather than by a test.

2. WHERE THE LEAK WILL APPEAR. ItemFilter searches Item.name only. The moment
somebody implements 'search identifiers', the natural DRF move is to annotate
the matched ItemIdentifier.value so the UI can show why a row matched. That
annotation, rendered as an option label, IS the three-spellings bug, and
nothing in the repo would stop it.

3. THE GUARD DOES NOT EXIST. No test pins 'the pulldown shows item names'.
test_catalogue_api asserts name is present, never that no identifier value is
present beside it. ItemList.test.tsx drives from a fixture, so a fixture
holding an identifier value would pass. Cheapest guard, and where it goes:
a test in test_catalogue_api.py beside test_items_can_be_searched_by_name that
mints a mis-cased identifier and recursively scans the JSON for it -- a
recursive scan rather than a field whitelist, because a whitelist passes a
future field named matched_on. Plus one in ItemList.test.tsx stubbing a row
that carries both. Not Playwright: one worker, shared seed, outside coverage.

4. THE PYTHON/SQL DISAGREEMENT HAS EXACTLY ONE LOAD-BEARING SITE, and strand 2
predicted it: _identifiers.py builds its dictionary keyed by
PostgreSQL's fold (read back off value_normalised) and looks it up with
Python's items.normalised(). Where the folds differ the lookup misses,
create() fires, the unique index raises, and because mint() is
transaction.atomic the WHOLE catalogue import aborts -- not one row. This is
decision 4's concrete cost.

Two tests claim to pin the Python/SQL agreement -- test_sheet_items.py and
test_sheet_people.py, both on lower() vs casefold() -- and NEITHER queries
PostgreSQL. A django_db test asserting value_normalised == items.normalised()
for the divergent characters would either pin it or prove strand 2 in CI.

5. VOLUNTEER FOLDING IS PYTHON-ONLY, and a docstring overstates it.
people.spelled() and addressed() lower their input and people.py claims this
matches 'the Lower(Trim()) column the identifier tables normalise with' --
but Volunteer.sheet_key and email have plain case-SENSITIVE unique indexes and
no generated column. No drift risk, because Python is the only fold; the
docstring's claim of parity is wrong and should be corrected.

6. AN INCONSISTENCY WORTH ITS OWN LINE: VolunteerFilter searches
email__iexact while volunteer_unique_email_when_present is case-sensitive. So
two rows differing only in the case of their address can both exist and one
search returns both.

7. Label.normalise_code is the model the identifier column is NOT following,
and it is the better one: normalise on write, store canonical, compare
exactly, over an ASCII-only alphabet a check constraint enforces. Worth citing
in the decision record as the shape that has no Python/SQL disagreement at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DECISION 5: confirmed. Nothing leaks, so the rule is a guard
to be written, not a bug to be fixed. Two cheap tests, named above.

title: A volunteer whose spelling moves is minted twice
description:
Found while fixing the review of PR #12, by the test test_a_spelling_that_stops_speaking_leaves_its_address_where_it_is, and deliberately not fixed there: no finding on that pull request raised it, and riding a fix along would have made one commit hold two issues.

When the spelling a volunteer's sheet_key is derived from stops appearing -- a name corrected in the export, or a rule 6 change that folds two spellings differently -- the next import mints a second row beside the first rather than recognising it. The report says 'volunteers 1, minted 1, already 0' while the table holds two, so the count and the database disagree and nothing says so.

Whether the answer is that the importer should recognise the row some other way, or that it should report the orphan and leave it for an administrator to merge, is the decision this bead makes. Note the batch's standing rule: the importer proposes and an administrator disposes, and it merges nobody.
acceptance_criteria: A volunteer whose sheet_key changes between runs does not silently become two rows, and whatever the importer does about it is a number in its report.

title: Run the import, and say what it did
description:
The command a contributor actually runs, and the report that makes the run reviewable: what was staged, what was minted, what was posted, and every row that reached none of those with the reason. profile_sheet says what the workbook contains; this says what the database now holds because of it.

The workbook is not ours to publish so nothing in CI reads it, and the same discipline profile_sheet is held to applies -- the figures come from the code that did the work rather than from prose, and the tests build their own workbook.

Closing this closes inventory-tng-2dg, which is what these five are.
acceptance_criteria: One command runs the whole import against a copy of the export, its report accounts for all 3,439 submissions, running it twice changes nothing, and it is covered by tests that need no workbook.

title: Post the ledger the staged rows describe
description:
One StockTransaction per batch that rule 5 finds, with a StockMovement per staged row inside it. Rule 2 decides which import as adjustment rather than as volunteer activity, rule 4 fills job_reference, and rule 3's locations are candidates only -- inventory-tng-o5t has not been to the meeting yet, so nothing here invents a Location.

Three things this has to answer rather than assume. Timestamps arrive naive and occasionally absent, and Submission.at says why; occurred_at is a DateTimeField under USE_TZ, so the importer decides the zone and records the decision. Quantities are floats in the sheet and a movement needs an integer, and decision 0011 section 6 says the packaging ambiguity must not be guessed -- import the value literally and flag the item. And the ledger is append-only with a trigger enforcing it, so a re-run must add nothing rather than fail.
acceptance_criteria: Every staged row reaches a movement or is recorded as one that could not, transactions group by rule 5, corrections import as adjustment, a second run posts nothing, and no quantity is multiplied by a guess.

title: Mint the volunteers rule 6 resolves, flags included
description:
people.directory() gives the volunteers the workbook holds and says which of them it is unsure of. Each becomes a Volunteer row; each flag becomes something an administrator can act on rather than a merge the importer performed.

The headcount is a range, 59 to 72, and the import mints the top of it -- merging only ever removes a row, and a merge sets merged_into and leaves the ledger untouched. A volunteer known only by an address is a row too, so the movement stays attributed to somebody an administrator can later name. Seven submissions reach nobody and this bead settles what happens to them.
acceptance_criteria: Every volunteer the directory names has a row, every flag is visible to an administrator without reading the importer's output, and a second run merges nobody and mints nobody twice.

title: Mint the identifiers rule 1 resolves
description:
Every item string that ever named an item becomes an ItemIdentifier, including the ones resolving to nothing. items.resolve() answers per string with how it resolved and, where it did not, why.

Unresolvable is imported as unresolvable rather than guessed at: the report's 'neither resolved nor accounted for' line is expected to stay at zero, and a string the catalogue does not hold must not silently acquire one. value_normalised is a Lower(Trim()) generated column and items._normalised already matches it, so the importer and the scan endpoint agree about what one identifier is.
acceptance_criteria: Every distinct item string in the export has an ItemIdentifier or a recorded reason it has none, a second run mints nothing new, and no string resolves to an item the rule said it does not name.

title: Stage the workbook's rows, keeping each one as it was
description:
Before anything is minted or posted, every row of the export lands in a staging table that keeps the source row verbatim as JSONB alongside the fields inventory/sheet/workbook.py read out of it. That is what makes the import re-runnable: a rule that changes re-reads the staged rows rather than the workbook, and a row that imported wrongly can be seen as it actually was.

Rows are keyed on the spreadsheet row number, which Submission.row already carries, so a second run updates rather than duplicates. Nothing here interprets anything -- the six rules run over the staged rows in the beads that follow.
acceptance_criteria: A management command stages every row of the export with its raw JSONB, running it twice leaves the same rows, and the staged rows are enough to re-run every rule without the workbook.

title: The report contract has no home of its own
description:
tuple[str, list[tuple[str, int]]] is written out in five places, and the Section alias that names it lives in the management command -- downstream of every module that implements it. So no rule module can reference its own contract, nothing type-checks a module against it until somebody adds it to SECTIONS, and a test reaching for the type has to import it from a command module, which is what test_brief_figures.py does.

Two things belong with it. population() is a sheet section living in the command rather than in the package, so 'every module in inventory.sheet exposes section(sheet)' is not true of the package and the importer cannot get the population report without importing a management command. And the convention that a label's indentation carries depth -- three spaces meaning 'a subset of the line above', not a third share -- is documented only at the one use site that needed it, where the author of rule 5 will not look.

The third row of the triage table: the contract is the composition of the command and four rule modules, and cannot be moved within any one of them. Raised by the simplify pass over the batch that introduced it, and worth doing before a82 and 5r2 write the type a sixth and seventh time.
acceptance_criteria: The report type is named once in inventory/sheet/, every section is annotated with it, population is a section of workbook.py like every other rule's, and the indentation convention is stated where the contract is.

Labels rather than numbers: the numbers come from the real export and cannot be in CI, but a section that gains, loses or renames a line is exactly what makes a pasted block stale.

The commit that moved the classifier figures out removed that composition from the Context in the same branch, so a closed bead certifies something the record no longer does. Its description also still asserts the withdrawn '18% -- 176 rows -- unambiguous volunteer returns', and its notes still defend 18.7%.

inventory-tng-o5t is open, P1 and meeting-facing. Its notes end 'Decision 0008's Context carries the same correction'; the Context now carries no location figure at all. It also quotes 205-across-31 with the compound predicate stripped, which the brief expressly forbids.

The batch caught and repaired this exact reversal for kx6 and missed both of these, which suggests the sweep needs to be by reference rather than by memory.
acceptance_criteria: Neither bead points at a claim the record no longer makes, and o5t carries its predicate with its figure.
notes: Closed 2026-08-21. 2a3's notes record that its close reason no longer holds and withdraw the 176-row figure; o5t carries the predicate for its 205-across-31 count and points at the brief.
close_reason: 2a3 records that its close reason no longer holds and withdraws the 176; o5t carries its predicate and points at the brief rather than a Context section that no longer holds a location figure.

title: The 65-people reading survives in ten places
description:
Decision 0008 used to say '102 spellings of 65 people'. The sheet classifiers brief now records that 65 is a count of distinct emails and not a headcount: 45% of submissions carry no email at all, 41 of the 102 spellings never appear beside one, and several of those are plainly separate people rather than variants. The real headcount is above 65 and nobody has established it.

The reading survives in ten places, six of them shipped source and two of them load-bearing architectural justifications:

  docs/data-model.md line 40, where 'around 65 people transact' is the stated reason Volunteer is not auth.User, and line 202, where it justifies the pg_trgm index
  docs/decisions/0015-merged-identifier-conflict.md line 25, the motivating example for that whole record
  backend/src/inventory/models.py line 152
  backend/src/inventory/tests/test_volunteers.py lines 4 and 462
  frontend/src/volunteers/VolunteerPicker.tsx line 8
  frontend/src/volunteers/rememberedVolunteer.ts line 5
  beads kx6, db4, ifh and 2dg

check-docs.sh reads only Markdown and the headers of scripts/, so nothing in CI will ever flag the code copies. Two of these are sizing arguments for design decisions, so the correction has to say whether the decision still holds at the real number rather than only swapping a figure.
acceptance_criteria: No file or bead states 65 as a headcount; each place either cites the distinct-email count as such or links to the brief, and the two sizing arguments say explicitly whether they still hold.
close_reason: Nine references corrected; data-model.md states the uncertainty once and links the brief, and both sizing arguments are noted as holding at either end of the range.

title: README and decision 0011 still route figures to 0008
description:
README.md line 25 promises 'Each of these is measured rather than assumed. The figures live once, in docs/decisions/0008#context'. That was true before the classifier-dependent figures moved to docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md, and is false now; README line 21's 'decision 0008 counts them' is false for the same reason, since 0008 now says only 'a large share'.

docs/decisions/0011-qr-batch-scanning.md lines 12-14 has the same break and is worse: it sends the reader to 0008#context for the burst figure and calls it the whole case for batching, but that figure is in Consequences rather than Context.

Only docs/data-model.md and 0008 itself link to the brief, so a contributor arriving through the README or through 0011 never learns it exists. The front door is the one place this most needs to work.
acceptance_criteria: README.md and decision 0011 describe where figures actually live and link to the brief; no document claims figures live somewhere they do not.
close_reason: README and 0011 now say which figures live in 0008 and which live in the brief, and both link to it.

title: Classifier: resolve a submission to a volunteer
description:
Rule 6 in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md. 102 distinct name spellings across the ledger, and the form asked for a name as free text every time.

The figure decision 0008 used to carry -- '102 spellings of 65 people' -- pairs a name count with an email count and reads as though 65 is a headcount. It is not: 45% of submissions carry no email at all, and 41 of the 102 spellings never appear beside one, several of them plainly separate people rather than variants. Case-folding names alone gives 86. The real headcount is above 65 and nobody knows it yet.

Establishing it is the deliverable. Duplicates that survive become Volunteer rows an administrator merges later, which the model already supports -- a merge sets merged_into and leaves the ledger untouched.
acceptance_criteria: A stated rule maps each submission to a volunteer, the brief carries the resulting headcount rather than an email count, and anything genuinely ambiguous imports flagged rather than silently merged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Classifier: group submissions into one batch
description:
Rule 5 in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md. The old form carried one item per submission, so a single trip to the shelf appears as a burst of rows; the new model records that as one StockTransaction with many movements. This decides where a burst starts and stops.

The rule is unsettled and the two obvious ones disagree. Chaining by gaps of ten minutes or less gives about 77% of submissions inside a burst and a largest burst of 24. A fixed ten-minute window anchored on the first submission gives about 76% but a largest of 17. Decision 0008 stated 76% and 24 together, which no single rule produces -- the halves came from different methods.

Also load-bearing: 45% of submissions carry no email, so which key identifies the submitter changes the answer. That interacts with the volunteer classifier.

At runtime this is already solved -- the cart is one transaction with many movements -- so this is migration-only.
acceptance_criteria: One rule is chosen, its window and its submitter key are both stated in the brief with the figures they produce, and the importer groups on it.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-21: this bead was filed saying decision 0008's '76% and 24' came from two different methods and that no single rule produces the pair. That is wrong. Chaining submissions by the same person on gaps of ten minutes or less gives a largest burst of 24 under every submitter key tried, and 76.6% inside a burst keying on email with a name fallback (76.8% by name, 77.8% by email alone). One rule produces both halves and 0008's figure reproduces.

What remains genuinely open is the submitter key, because 45% of submissions carry no email, and whether to chain on gaps or anchor a fixed window -- the latter gives a largest burst of 17, so the window rule is what decides that figure.

Also: it blocks two P2 beads (inventory-tng-2dg and inventory-tng-6s9), so it is P2 itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: Classifier: pull a job reference out of a note
description:
Rule 4 in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md, and the simplest of the six: a note containing NN followed by digits names a job. 136 submissions cite one, across 54 distinct numbers.

Becomes StockTransaction.job_reference, a field that already exists, so after the import nothing has to read prose to answer 'what went into NN217'. At runtime the batch endpoint already accepts it, so this is migration-only.
acceptance_criteria: Imported transactions carry job_reference where the note names one, and the count is emitted by profile_sheet.
notes: Blocks two P2 beads (inventory-tng-2dg and inventory-tng-6s9), so it is P2 itself; a blocker filed below the work it blocks does not surface in bd ready when it needs to.
close_reason: Closed

title: Classifier: resolve an item string to a catalogued item
description:
Rule 1 in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md. Decides, for each of the 145 distinct item strings, which catalogued item it names -- or that it names none.

The sheet's own lookup is a VLOOKUP against the catalogue and VLOOKUP is case-insensitive, so a string differing only in case already resolves today. Nine strings are case-only variants covering 172 submissions; 32 match nothing at all across 83 submissions; 52 are retired NYCM codes across 125.

The trap to avoid: the largest unmatched string is TP-Link SFP-RJ45 at 40 submissions, and the catalogue holds SFP-RJ45 Module separately. That is an alias, not a typo, and the two readings mint different ItemIdentifier rows. Whoever builds this decides that per string rather than by regex.

Highest runtime value of the six: the same resolution lets a volunteer type what they actually call the thing.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 145 strings resolves to a catalogued item or is explicitly recorded as unresolvable, the rule is stated in the brief, and the partition is emitted by profile_sheet rather than counted by hand.
close_reason: Closed

title: Classifier: extract a location from a note
description:
Rule 3 in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md. The old sheet had no location concept, so people wrote places into the notes field; this recovers them into Location rows and the from/to sides of imported movements.

Case handling is the open question and it changes the answer materially: one room at 131 Broome is written 31 ways across 205 submissions counting case-sensitively, or 24 ways folding case. Notes mentioning any mesh room, including a different site entirely, total 231 across 41 -- a figure that has already been misused once for this room.

Seeds inventory-tng-o5t, which carries the real location list to the meeting.
acceptance_criteria: A stated rule turns notes into candidate locations, its figures are in the brief, and what it extracts is offered to o5t as a seed rather than imported unreviewed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Classifier: decide whether a note is a correction
description:
Rule 2 in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md. Decides which historical rows import as adjustment rather than as volunteer activity -- which is what makes attribution reporting mean anything, per decision 0008 supporting decision 4.

The rule is genuinely unsettled and the brief says so. Whole-note equality against the four enumerated strings gives 406 rows, 11.8%. Substring matching double-counts, since 'inventory correct' contains 'inventory correction'. A broad regex gives about 21%. Decision 0008 previously asserted 18.7%, which reproduces under none of them and whose original method is unrecorded.

Settling this is the deliverable, not the number. Until it is settled the four exact counts are the only reproducible part.
design: Containment runs the other way than the description says: 'inventory correction' contains 'inventory correct'. A substring match therefore double-counts the 67 correction rows, which are the ones to guard.
acceptance_criteria: One rule is chosen and written into the brief with the count it produces, the decision between whole-note and substring matching is justified, and 2dg imports on that rule.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-21: the description states the substring containment backwards. 'inventory correction' contains 'inventory correct', not the reverse. For whoever implements it: a substring match sweeps each of the 67 'inventory correction' rows up twice, so those are the rows to guard, not the 50 'inventory correct' ones.
close_reason: Closed

title: Report the sheet's figures by running the classifiers
description:
A management command, profile_sheet, that takes a path to the exported workbook, runs every classifier in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md over it, and prints the breakdown each one produces.

This is what makes the brief's figures reproducible rather than asserted. The workbook is not ours to publish and is gitignored, so nothing in CI can read the real file; the command is unit-tested against a small synthetic fixture instead, and the real numbers come from a contributor running it against their own copy.

The point is not the report. It is that a figure in the brief and the behaviour of the importer come from the same code, so they cannot drift apart -- which is the failure this whole line of work exists to stop. Three review passes over one batch each found hand-written figures that no longer matched anything.
acceptance_criteria: profile_sheet emits every figure the brief states, the brief cites the command rather than a hand count, and the command is covered by tests that run without the real workbook.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two beads still quote figures the batch retracted
description:
inventory-tng-8sq and inventory-tng-o5t were written before the export was checked and still carry figures the rest of the batch withdrew. Neither was touched by the commits that did the withdrawing, so this is a defect in work those commits did not make rather than part of either.

8sq, which owns the stakeholder guide, asserted that 54% of equipment check-outs carry a note and 13% name a node -- measured 61% (1,494 of 2,455) and 5% (131 of 2,455) -- and led with the 68% cable claim that inventory-tng-2zx supersedes.

o5t, which carries the location list to the meeting, quoted 'Sean mesh room 131 broome st' (175 rows). That exact string appears 97 times; the room is written 31 ways across 205 rows.

Both are open and meeting-facing, so a stale figure here reaches people rather than sitting in history.
acceptance_criteria: Neither bead states a figure the batch retracted, and each carries the corrected one with the same method the record now names.
notes: Corrected figures verified against the export on 2026-08-21 by the method decision 0008 now names.
close_reason: 8sq and o5t now carry the measured figures; both descriptions rewritten.

title: Say what the sheet's 984 check-ins actually are
description:
Decision 0008's Context cites '2,455 check-outs against 984 check-ins' and draws the right conclusion from it -- returning costs more effort than taking, because every printed QR encodes a form link hardcoded to Checking Out. What it does not say is what those 984 rows contain, and the gap is load-bearing: a reader takes 'check-in' to mean a volunteer bringing something back, and that reading is wrong four times out of five.

Classified by what each note says, the 984 are 39% corrections (Fixing Inventory, Updating inventory), 21% order receipts, 23% blank and therefore unclassifiable, and 18% -- 176 rows in four years -- unambiguous volunteer returns.

This strengthens the argument already in the Context rather than changing it, and it forecloses a specific mistake. Reading return behaviour out of the check-in column produced a per-item custody proposal that did not survive checking (inventory-tng-8sq, reopened; inventory-tng-2zx notes carry the reproduction). The correction belongs beside the statistic it qualifies so the next reader does not repeat it.

Independent of how Q1 is eventually answered: it is a fact about the export, not about custody.
acceptance_criteria: Decision 0008's Context says what the 984 check-ins are composed of, sourced from the export, and the figure is reproducible from the workbook by the method the record names.
notes:
Reproduced from ignored/NYC Mesh - Inventory Sheet.xlsx tab QRresponses (3,456 rows) on 2026-08-20. The 18.7% corrections figure already in the Context is measured over the whole ledger; the 39% here is measured over check-ins only, so the two are consistent rather than competing and the record should not let them read as a contradiction.

--- THIS BEAD'S CLOSE REASON NO LONGER HOLDS, 2026-08-21 ---

Closed on 'Decision 0008's Context now states the composition of the 984 check-ins'. Inventory-tng-hr2 later removed that composition from the Context, because the shares rested on a correction rule that is not settled. What 0008 now says is that a check-in cannot be read as return behaviour in either direction, which is the claim this bead was actually raised to establish, so the point survives even though the sentence certifying it does not.

The description's '18% -- 176 rows -- unambiguous volunteer returns' is withdrawn. That figure named a residual bucket rather than a measurement: only 68 of those rows say anything came back. The defence of 18.7% in these notes is likewise superseded -- docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md records that it reproduces under no rule tried.
close_reason: Decision 0008's Context now states the composition of the 984 check-ins, reproducible from the export's QRresponses tab.

title: Enforce per-item custody: the opening half, and the toggle
description:
inventory-tng-2zx records WHICH items are worth chasing, as data. This is the machinery that makes that field mean something, and it is three pieces of work rather than one.

1. The opening half, as an invariant. A check-out of a custody-tracked item must land in a location of kind volunteer_custody, never NULL. This is the same shape as inventory_movement_matches_kind in migration 0008 -- the movement's own columns checked against another row's flag -- with one more join, movement -> item. It passes decision 0016's test for belonging in the database: an administrator writing deliberately should be refused too, because a check-out of a chased item evaporating to NULL is a hole in the data whoever wrote it. So it binds the admin, fixtures and the sheet importer, not only the API.

2. Refusing the toggle when it would strand stock. Flipping an item from chased to consumed while it has non-zero balances in custody locations leaves those balances with no legal way to close. This repository has already met this defect and settled its shape: inventory-tng-ai0 refused merging or retiring a volunteer who holds an active custody location, naming it, rather than leaving it orphaned. The toggle behaves the same way, and says what to do first. Its sibling question, what active=False means for stock still on the shelf, is inventory-tng-6c7.

3. Which point in time the rule is judged at. A trigger fires when a row is written, against the flag as it stands then -- but occurred_at can be in the past. A batch filled while an item was consumed-at-checkout and saved after the flip would be judged by the new rule and refused, and the sheet migration (inventory-tng-2dg) writes 3,439 rows that all predate any flip. Item already carries HistoricalRecords, so 'was this item custody-tracked on the date this movement happened' is answerable without a new effective-from column. Deciding this belongs here, not in the middle of the import.

Existing history is never invalidated by a flip either way: the ledger is append-only, so a toggle governs only the shape of new rows.
acceptance_criteria: A check-out of a custody-tracked item cannot reach NULL from any writer; flipping an item to consumed while stock sits in custody is refused and names what blocks it; and the point in time the rule is judged at is decided and documented rather than assumed.
notes: Raised while settling inventory-tng-8sq. Interacts with inventory-tng-c6s (what occurred_at should be for a batch saved long after it was filled), which must be settled before piece 3 can be implemented rather than merely specified.

title: Show open custody at a glance, so cleaning it up is easy
description:
The closing half of a custody check-out is human: no trigger can make a volunteer walk back and scan a return or a consumption. What the system CAN do is make the gap trivially visible, so that an administrator running a sweep -- or any volunteer who offers to help tidy up -- can act without constructing a query.

Balances are already a plain database view (docs/data-model.md#balances). This is that view restricted to locations of kind volunteer_custody and given an age: '3 x foo, held by Sean, 47 days'. Grouped both ways, by person and by item, because the two cleanups are different jobs -- 'what am I still holding' is a volunteer asking about themselves, 'what is outstanding on cable' is someone chasing one item.

This is what turns the admin-reconciliation fallback from theoretically possible into something that actually happens. Decision 0008's counter-argument to custody tracking is that skipped workflows produce balances that drift upward and are worse than no tracking at all. Drift that is visible, attributed and aged is a work queue; the same drift unsurfaced is the thing 0008 warns about.
acceptance_criteria: Anyone can see every unclosed custody holding, aged, grouped by volunteer and by item, and act on it without writing a query or opening the admin.
notes: Raised while settling inventory-tng-8sq. The reconciliation itself is already expressible: decision 0011 section 6 has consumption requiring a from_location and forbidding a to_location, so custody:Sean -> NULL is well formed, and adjustments and counts constrain nothing deliberately. StockTransaction.actor records who posted it and kind separates a genuine consumption from an administrator's adjustment, so leaning on the fallback does not repeat the sheet's 18.7% of corrections masquerading as volunteer activity.

title: Batch: the checkers' remaining papercuts
description:
Five leftovers from the three tooling batches: a receipt nothing ignores, a checker that reports one long line at a time, an epic counted as work, a read boundary that is a glob rather than the principle, and the squash nobody can see.

Chosen to test the finding from the last measurement: three of these touch scripts/check-commit.sh or DEVELOPERS.md, but in different regions of each. If adjacency rather than file identity is what costs, this should collapse with few conflicts despite the shared files.
close_reason: All five landed in pull request 5.

title: Catch a squash after the fact, since the flag cannot be read
description:
repo-settings.sh --check cannot read allow_squash_merge from a safely-scoped CI token: GitHub's docs say merge-related settings need contents:read AND contents:write, so a token that could check them could also push code. That is not a trade worth making for a drift check, and the current 'this token cannot read the merge methods' line should say so as a deliberate limit rather than a missing permission.

Merge commits are already covered -- required_linear_history blocks them and that IS readable. The gap is squash merge: re-enabled, it would flatten a batch into one commit, which is what this workflow exists to prevent, and nothing would notice.

It is detectable after the fact with no extra permission: run check-batch.sh over main's recent commits in the weekly job. A squashed batch shows up as one commit closing several issues, which is exactly what that script refuses. Detection the Monday after beats never.

Also worth saying in DEVELOPERS.md that the merge-method half is unreadable by design, so nobody grants a write-scoped token chasing it. I told the maintainer to add Contents: Read-only before checking the docs; it does nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The weekly job refuses a commit on main that closes more than one issue, and DEVELOPERS.md says why the merge flags are not checked.
close_reason: The weekly job asks whether any recent commit on main closes more than one issue, which is what a squashed batch looks like once landed.

title: Batch: the scanner and the retired row
description: Five product issues: three in the scanning path and two in the catalogue API. Chosen to sit in disjoint files, as a test of whether autosquash conflict cost is driven by bead count or by file overlap.
close_reason: Landed.
